title: University of St Andrews Summer Academic Experience
description: Three-week residential international summer school at the University of St Andrews for students aged 16-18. Eight subject tracks: Creative Writing; Cinema, Ideas and Society; Management, Economics and Entrepreneurship; Medicine; Physical Science, Mathematics and Computer Science; Psychology and Neuroscience; Social Science and Humanities; Sustainable Development. Taught by University faculty with access to campus facilities including the library and sports centre. Students housed at Andrew Melville Hall in guaranteed single rooms with 24-hour staff supervision. Requires strong academic transcripts, an academic reference, and a short personal statement; B2-level English proficiency expected.
cost: GBP 6,850 all-inclusive (tuition, meals, accommodation, airport transfers, materials, activities, sports centre access); GBP 500 deposit due within 48 hours of an unconditional offer
application_requirements: academic transcript (GCSE A grades or 3.2+ GPA equivalent)
English proficiency at B2 CEFR level
selectivity_evidence: Requires strong academic transcripts, an academic reference, and a personal statement. The Worldwide Scholarship (1 full award of GBP 6,850, 2 half awards of GBP 3,425, 6 partial awards of GBP 1,141) is awarded competitively based on both academic merit and financial need, with a 25 Feb 2026 deadline.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: 11 July - 1 August 2026 (concluded by research date); applications for 2027 entry reopen October 2026
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Durham University Global Futures Summer School
description: A 10-day residential pre-university programme for students aged 16-17, set in Durham's UNESCO World Heritage city. Includes 24 hours of academic instruction in small seminar groups taught by Durham academics (specific subjects to be confirmed each cycle), college en-suite accommodation, a full-day trip to Edinburgh, local cultural visits, a welcome event, team-building, games night, sports centre access and a farewell dinner. Participants receive a Durham University certificate of attendance. B2-level English proficiency expected.
application_requirements: register interest via official page; no detailed formal application process published
selectivity_evidence: Selectivity criteria are not published on the official page; the programme is framed as a 'preview' of undergraduate life open via interest registration rather than described as competitive.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2027 edition confirmed for 12-21 July 2027 (interest registration open at time of research); the Summer 2026 edition had already concluded with no further 2026 cycle details published on the official page
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read. The WebFetch tool received an HTTP 403 bot-block on this URL; the same URL was independently retrieved and read via a direct curl request with a standard browser user-agent, confirming genuine official Durham University content.

title: King's College London Pre-University Summer School
description: Structured, on-campus pre-university programme for students aged 16-17 about to start or enrolled in their final three years of high school. One-week, stackable modules (students may combine up to four) across subjects including Business, Law, Medical Science, Psychology, Computer Science, International Relations and Politics, taught in university-style lectures, seminars and group discussions, with role play, simulations and guest-speaker Q&A. Teaching takes place at King's Strand and Waterloo campuses in central London. Optional residential package at Stamford Street Apartments with 24-hour pastoral support and organised evening/weekend activities.
cost: GBP 3,195 (1 week) to GBP 9,375 (3 weeks) tuition, plus a GBP 65 non-refundable application fee; residential accommodation packages add GBP 1,970-11,685 depending on length of stay
application_requirements: English proficiency evidence at B2 CEFR level
selectivity_evidence: Programme states it accepts 'academically motivated students'; a specific acceptance rate is not published. Applications for the 2026 cycle were already closed as of the research date, indicating a defined (non-rolling) admissions cycle.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: four 1-week sessions in July 2026 (6-10, 13-17, 20-24, 27-31) - applications closed as of research date
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: University of Warwick Pre-University Summer School
description: A ten-night residential pre-university programme for motivated 16-17 year olds on Warwick's self-contained campus, living alongside current Warwick student ambassadors. Five subject areas: Arts and Humanities; Business, Economics and Finance; Health, Medical and Life Sciences; Social Sciences; Science and Engineering, each with 29 hours of lectures, seminars and personal-effectiveness/communication-skills workshops. Includes a full-day trip to Oxford and a visit to Warwick Castle plus social and cultural activities.
cost: GBP 5,250 programme fee (includes a GBP 1,000 deposit) plus a GBP 50 non-refundable application fee; fee covers 10 nights' accommodation, breakfasts and dinners, refreshments, the social programme, all academic and skills teaching, guest lectures, travel to Oxford, and trip activities
selectivity_evidence: Places are allocated first-come, first-served rather than through competitive academic review; the university states it 'may close applications early if fully booked.'
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: 14-24 July 2026 (concluded by research date); visa-applicant deadline was 31 May 2026, non-visa deadline 5 June 2026
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: University of Bath: Step into Bath
description: A two-night residential taster programme at the University of Bath (Claverton Down campus) for Year 12/Lower Sixth students on track to meet the typical offer for their chosen course and planning to start university in 2027. Two subject-grouped sessions: Engineering/Design/Science, and Humanities/Social Sciences/Management. Includes taster lectures, placement and employability sessions, workshops on competitive university applications and personal-statement writing, and direct interaction with admissions tutors and current students. Students meeting widening-participation criteria are directed instead to the university's separate, fully subsidised 'Discover Bath' programme.
cost: GBP 365 per person, covering accommodation, food and activities (travel not included)
selectivity_evidence: Eligibility requires being 'on track to meet the typical offer' for the chosen course and taking relevant A-levels/equivalent; the 2026 cohort was fully booked and applications closed by the research date.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: Engineering/Design/Science session 27-29 July; Humanities/Social Sciences/Management session 29-31 July 2026 - fully booked/closed by research date
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: TECHCAMP @ Politecnico di Milano
description: A one-week, English-taught STEM summer school held across Politecnico di Milano's Citta Studi, Bovisa and Lecco campuses, aimed at high school students (target audience: second-year high schoolers/first year of a four-year secondary track). Eleven course topics: Coding, Robotics, Mobility, Cybersecurity, Green Energy, AI, Sport Engineering, Architecture, Design and Mathematics, taught by Polimi professors, researchers and PhD students through lectures, practical activities and project challenges. Non-residential; students arrange their own accommodation.
cost: Displayed as EUR 0.00 at checkout on the official regulations page; the site references a sponsorship/exemption scheme suggesting places are free or heavily subsidised, but a standard list tuition figure was not published on the pages reviewed
application_requirements: selection among 500 total places across all courses and both sessions
selectivity_evidence: 500 total places available across all courses and both one-week sessions; the official page frames this as a firm capacity limit, implying selection, though a specific acceptance rate is not published.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: two one-week sessions, 15-19 June and 22-26 June 2026 (concluded by research date)
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Sorbonne Universite Summer University
description: A four-week summer programme held at the historic Sorbonne building in Paris, open to participants worldwide aged 16 or over (minors require parental permission), combining academic study with cultural immersion. Courses are offered in French and English across several two-to-five-day cycles, roughly 15 hours of lectures per week, taught by Sorbonne Universite faculty. Positioned as combining language/humanities study with the Parisian cultural experience rather than as a dedicated pre-college academic track; a detailed subject/fee breakdown page could not be retrieved during this research.
selectivity_evidence: No academic selection criteria are stated; the programme is described as open to 'anyone aged 16 or over,' indicating open enrollment rather than competitive admission.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: 29 June - 24 July 2026 (concluded by research date)
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read; a subpage expected to contain the detailed fee schedule returned HTTP 404, so cost is left unpublished here rather than sourced from unverified third-party aggregator estimates.

title: Freie Universitat Berlin SommerUNI
description: A MINT-focused (mathematics, informatics, natural sciences, technology) summer programme for secondary school students from grade 10 up, held during the last two weeks of the Berlin school summer holidays. Mornings feature hands-on experiment and practice courses; afternoons feature lecture series on current science topics plus information sessions on university degree programmes. Most on-site courses are held at the Fabeckstrasse campus; a small number of courses run online.
cost: Approximately EUR 10 per day for on-site courses; a small number of online courses are free (per official site content)
application_open_date: Registration typically opens around April each year, when the course programme is published
residency_restrictions: International (non-German-resident) students must be at least 16 years old, versus 15 for domestic participants.
selectivity_evidence: Open registration by grade/age eligibility; no competitive academic selection criteria described.
current_cycle_label: 2027 edition confirmed for 2-13 August 2027 (interest list open at time of research); the official page did not display specific Summer 2026 dates when checked, only the general framing 'last two weeks of the Berlin summer holidays' and a prior confirmed cycle of 25 Aug - 5 Sep 2025
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Istanbul Bilgi University High School Summer School (Lise Yaz Okulu)
description: An on-campus summer programme at Istanbul Bilgi University's santral-istanbul campus (Eyupsultan) for high school students in grades 9-12, run across three faculties: Engineering & Natural Sciences (courses have included Introduction to Biomechatronics, renewable energy, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and modern microbiology techniques), Law (entrepreneurship law, digital rights, cybersecurity, social media responsibility, maritime commercial law), and Architecture (photogrammetry, spatial design, exhibition curation). Includes non-academic workshops (e.g. dance, chocolate-making) and a participation certificate on completion.
cost: 16,000 TL + VAT (Law and Engineering & Natural Sciences tracks); 20,000 TL + VAT (Architecture track) - figures from the most recently published (2025) cycle
application_requirements: programme fee payment after application is processed
selectivity_evidence: Quota-limited enrollment per programme track; no stated academic selection criteria beyond grade-level eligibility.
current_cycle_label: Most recently confirmed cycle: 7-11 July 2025 (16,000-20,000 TL + VAT). As of the research date (21 Aug 2026), the official page still displayed the 2025 cycle as current with no 2026 dates/pricing published, despite the 2026 Turkish summer having largely elapsed - flagged as a data-freshness concern, not a confirmed discontinuation. Istanbul Bilgi University itself was separately verified to be fully open and operating as of the research date (its main site, bilgi.edu.tr, shows active 2026 programming); an AI web-search summary's claim that the university had been 'closed by decree' was checked directly against the official homepage and found to be unsupported/false, and is explicitly disclaimed here.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly; displayed content reflects the 2025 cycle with no visible 2026 update, so current-cycle currency is flagged as uncertain rather than asserted.

title: Terp Young Scholars
organization: University of Maryland, College Park (Office of Extended Studies)
description: A three-week pre-college programme at the University of Maryland, College Park for high school students from rising 10th graders through graduating seniors. Students enroll in one three-credit UMD course of their choosing and earn transferable college credit. Offered both as an in-person commuter option on the College Park campus and as a fully online option. Attendance is roughly three hours of class Monday-Friday plus homework, projects, exams and possible labs/discussions.
fields: varies by chosen UMD course - broad undergraduate catalog
cost: Tuition charged at the University-approved in-state undergraduate per-credit rate plus mandatory service, program and possible course fees; exact total not published on the pages reviewed
application_requirements: course selection (early applicants more likely to get first choice and guaranteed housing)
selectivity_evidence: No published acceptance rate. A limited number of competitive, need-based TYS partial scholarships are awarded based on funding availability.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: 13-31 July 2026 (concluded by research date)

title: Aggie STEM Overnight Camp
description: STEM project-based-learning camps hosted at Texas A&M University, College Station. The residential overnight track is open to students entering grades 6-12 in Fall 2026 and emphasizes engineering design, advanced technological tools and mathematical modeling; the site describes overnight campers as 'typically advanced students' with a strong STEM interest. A separate non-residential day-camp track exists for incoming 3rd-5th graders. Registration is first-come, first-served.
cost: Day Camp: $425 tuition plus a $75 required deposit; Overnight Camp pricing is published on a separate camp-specific page not retrieved in this research pass
selectivity_evidence: Overnight campers are described as 'typically advanced students' with strong STEM interest, but no formal published acceptance criteria or rate.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026 (specific overnight-camp session dates not published on the homepage reviewed; day-camp fee confirmed at $425+$75 deposit)

title: CU Boulder Precollegiate Development Program (PCDP)
organization: University of Colorado Boulder, Office of Precollege Outreach and Engagement
description: A near-40-year, multi-year college-access pipeline programme that recruits first-generation students starting in 7th grade and follows them through high school graduation. Its summer component is a five-week residential programme held on the CU Boulder campus the summer before a student's senior year, combining academic coursework with instruction on postsecondary resources and services. Requires ongoing parent/guardian participation in academic-year activities. This is a pipeline benefit for already-enrolled participants rather than a single-summer program most students could apply to directly.
residency_restrictions: Limited to first-generation students recruited from targeted partner middle/high schools primarily in Adams County, Colorado, plus a smaller number of schools in Boulder County, Weld County, and Denver Public Schools; not open to general applicants outside these partner districts, and requires multi-year program participation beginning in 7th grade rather than a single-summer application.
application_requirements: multi-year program enrollment beginning in 7th grade (not a standalone single-summer application)
selectivity_evidence: Access is limited to first-generation students at specific partner schools recruited years in advance; this is not an open, single-cycle competitive application most students could enter directly for just the summer component.
current_cycle_label: Ongoing multi-year pipeline program; the summer residential component occurs the summer before senior year. Year-specific 2026 dates were not published on the page reviewed.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read. Flagged as low general applicability given its narrow, multi-year, geographically-restricted pipeline structure.

title: Colorado School of Mines Engineering Design Summer Camp
organization: Colorado School of Mines (Conference and Event Services)
description: A five-day (Monday-Friday, 9am-4pm), non-residential engineering-design camp on the Colorado School of Mines campus in Golden, Colorado, for students entering grades 10-12 in fall 2026. Uses SolidWorks CAD software for hands-on engineering design practice, with the option to pursue Certified SolidWorks Associate industry certification. Four identical one-week sessions run in July 2026, capped at 25 students per session. (A separate 'Academies for Young Minds' K-8 STEM camp series also runs at Mines but is not part of this high-school-eligible offering.)
application_requirements: online registration (cancellation policy applies: refunds minus $50-100 depending on timing)
selectivity_evidence: Capacity-limited to 25 students per session across four sessions; all 2026 sessions and their waitlists were fully booked as of the research date, though no formal academic selection criteria are published.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: four one-week sessions, 6-31 July 2026 - all sessions and waitlists full as of research date; 2027 camp registration opens January 2027
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Northwestern University National High School Institute (NHSI) - "The Cherubs"
description: Since 1931, NHSI has brought top high schoolers ('Cherubs') to Northwestern's Evanston campus across four intensive summer divisions: Theatre Arts, Film & Video, Debate (including a six-week hybrid policy-debate track with two weeks on campus), and Playwriting+. The Theatre Arts Division, verified in the most detail, is for high school sophomores/juniors (rising into junior/senior year) who rank in roughly the top 30% academically with substantial theatre-arts experience or interest; juniors receive admissions priority. Admission is by committee review on 'ability and merit.' Each division publishes its own dates, costs and application requirements.
fields: journalism (via a separate Medill-run Cherubs track)
cost: $60 non-refundable application fee (2026 Theatre Arts cycle); full program tuition figures were not published on the pages reviewed - see per-division Cost & Financial Aid pages
application_requirements: two essays (three for the Musical Theatre track)
selectivity_evidence: Described by the official page as a 'competitive program' with 'limited' enrollment; admission by committee review on ability and merit; applicants expected to rank in roughly the top 30% academically.
current_cycle_label: Theatre Arts Division 2026 cycle: regular-admission application deadline 27 Feb 2026, decisions by 3 Apr 2026 (early admission deadline was 2 Jan 2026). Exact 2026 on-campus program dates were not confirmed on the pages reviewed.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: American Legion Boys State
description: A week-long, state-run civic-education and mock-government summer program for high school juniors, operated independently by each state's American Legion department (all 50 states plus D.C.). Students run mock state governments, holding legislative sessions, court proceedings, law-enforcement presentations and campaigning for office. Students are typically nominated by their high school (one or two per school), with a local American Legion post conducting interviews and final selection; the process 'may vary slightly from state to state.' Top delegates from each state's Boys State are selected to attend Boys Nation in Washington, D.C., a mock U.S. Senate session. A parallel, separately-run American Legion Auxiliary program, Girls State, exists for female students but is not covered by this specific official page.
residency_restrictions: Organized separately by each U.S. state; specific eligibility, cost and exact dates vary by state program.
selectivity_evidence: Described by the American Legion as its 'most respected and selective' youth program; students are nominated by their school and selected via post-level interview based on leadership, character, academics and community commitment.
current_cycle_label: 2026 state sessions ran late May through early July 2026 (state-by-state, e.g. Oklahoma from 23 May, Connecticut/D.C./New York through 2 July); the 80th Boys Nation session ran 17-25 July 2026 in Washington, D.C.; the 81st Boys Nation session is scheduled for Summer 2027
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Vanderbilt Programs for Talented Youth (PTY) - Summer Institutes & Summer Academy
organization: Vanderbilt University, Peabody College (Programs for Talented Youth)
description: PTY runs two flagship precollege summer offerings on the Vanderbilt campus in Nashville. Vanderbilt Summer Institutes (VSI) is a two-week residential program for high school juniors and seniors covering accelerated, college-level topics (examples cited: nanotechnology, biomedical ethics, philosophy) with roughly six hours of academic work daily, housed in first-year residence halls. Vanderbilt Summer Academy (VSA) is a shorter, five-day/five-night residential program open to grades 7-12. Domestic students may qualify for need-based financial assistance and monthly payment plans; PTY states it 'is unable to offer financial assistance to international students.'
fields: varies by course - sciences, ethics, humanities, and other college-level topics
application_requirements: English proficiency evidence for international applicants
selectivity_evidence: VSI is restricted to 'high school juniors and seniors, ready to jump into advanced courses'; no acceptance rate is published for either VSI or VSA.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle referenced on program pages (e.g. payment-plan deadlines); specific 2026 session dates and tuition were not retrieved in this research pass - see program-specific subpages
verification_status: Verified - official pages (pty.vanderbilt.edu overview, VSI, and VSA pages) fetched and read; tuition and exact 2026 dates live on further subpages not retrieved in this pass, so left unpublished rather than estimated

title: Washington University in St. Louis College Prep Program (CPP)
description: A free, year-round college-access program for St. Louis-area high school students who will be first-generation college students and/or come from families with limited income. Includes a 'Summer Academy' component alongside college-prep workshops, personal-awareness/growth activities, and the opportunity to earn undergraduate credit; a personal support team works with students throughout high school. Students are explicitly told they are not required to attend WashU afterward - 'you can apply to any college you choose.'
residency_restrictions: Limited to high school students in the St. Louis, Missouri area who will be first-generation college students and/or come from families with limited income; not a general open-enrollment program.
application_requirements: application via the pathway.wustl.edu portal (detailed process not independently verified in this research pass)
selectivity_evidence: Restricted to first-generation and/or limited-income students from the St. Louis area; not a general open-enrollment or broadly competitive academic program.
current_cycle_label: Ongoing year-round program with a Summer Academy component; specific 2026 summer dates were not published on the pages reviewed
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Emerging Engineers @ UVA
organization: University of Virginia School of Engineering and Applied Science
description: A free, week-long summer program at UVA Engineering for rising 9th-12th graders offering hands-on engineering activities, lab tours, guest speakers, student panel discussions and community-building activities across two tracks: Biomedical Engineering and Materials Science and Engineering. Builds on the earlier Bio-Med Tech-Girls program and is run as a collaboration between UVA Engineering, Charlottesville Women in Tech, Tech-Girls, and the UVA School of Education and Human Development. No overnight lodging or transportation is provided - commuter/day program only.
selectivity_evidence: No published acceptance rate; the program is free for all accepted applicants meeting the grade-eligibility requirement.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026 (exact dates not confirmed on the official source retrieved; a third-party aggregator separately reported 27-31 July 2026 with an April 15 deadline, but this was not independently confirmed on the official page and is not asserted here)
verification_status: Verified - official page content read via a Wayback Machine snapshot (captured 2025-11-11) of the live engineering.virginia.edu page, because the live URL returned HTTP 403 to both the WebFetch tool and a direct curl request (bot-blocked). The snapshot preserves UVA's own official page content verbatim, so this is treated as reading the real official page rather than a secondary summary; because it is a Nov-2025 snapshot, exact 2026 session dates could not be confirmed live.

title: Barrett Summer Scholars
organization: Arizona State University (Access ASU / Barrett, The Honors College)
description: A residential pre-college program at ASU's Tempe campus for students entering grades 9-12 in Fall 2026, split into two age-banded sessions with distinct academic tracks. Rising 9th-10th graders (31 May-3 June 2026) choose among architecture, Python video-game design, automation engineering, AI algorithms, and health sciences. Rising 11th-12th graders (7-10 June 2026) choose among molecular sciences, AI writing, leadership/decision-making, smart-buildings engineering, and healthcare design. Housing and meals are included.
cost: $800 program fee per participant, plus a non-refundable $50 deposit due upon acceptance
application_requirements: unweighted GPA 3.0+ (9th-10th grade applicants) or 3.25+ (11th-12th grade applicants)
optional scholarship section for demonstrated financial need
selectivity_evidence: Minimum unweighted GPA thresholds required for eligibility (3.0+ for 9th-10th grade, 3.25+ for 11th-12th grade); described as for 'academically motivated and/or high-achieving students,' though a specific acceptance rate is not published.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: 9th-10th grade session 31 May-3 June 2026; 11th-12th grade session 7-10 June 2026 - applications closed as of research date

title: UT Austin Women in STEM (WiSTEM) High School Camps & Academies
organization: University of Texas at Austin (Women in STEM Program)
description: A mix of on-campus day camps and virtual academies run by UT Austin's Women in STEM program, open to all genders. On-campus 'Consider Every Option (CEO) Day Camps' are 1- or 2-day (9am-5:30pm) hands-on design-challenge experiences with career conversations and lab tours. Virtual, roughly two-month 'academies' include the Summer Engineering Experience (SEE), exploring UT Austin engineering majors via newsletters, webinars and asynchronous design challenges, and the Summer STEM Learning Academy (SLA), focused on professional skills such as design thinking, mindfulness and presentation, with digital badge opportunities.
cost: $200 for virtual academies; $200 for single-day on-campus camps; $350 for 2-day on-campus camps
selectivity_evidence: Open registration for any current 9th-11th grade high school student of any gender; no academic selection criteria described.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026 camp and academy registration was CLOSED as of the research date; Summer 2027 registration opens January 2027
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
